clue.text: Fear landing accident may be the big finish

indicators.note: an accident throws things into disorder, so these letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A crash on touchdown would be a dramatic way to end a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' is the anagram signal; FEARLANDING rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The climax of a show or concert is its final grand number, its spectacular closing piece.

clue.text: Having the hump

parts.note: British slang for being sulky, but read literally it describes a shape bulging out like a hunched back or a nearly full moon

explanation.walkthrough: 'Having the hump' is British slang for being in a bad mood; the literal sense of a bulge or swelling is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Convex or humped in outline, like a moon more than half lit or a hunchback.

clue.text: New cadet deputised

indicators.note: a new version of the word cadet means its letters arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A freshly recruited officer trainee stood in for someone senior.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to stand in or perform a role on behalf of another, as an actor plays a part.

clue.text: Go fishing, but keep in touch

explanation.surface: An angler heads off to the river but promises to stay in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting a hook on a cord is angling; sending someone a short letter or note maintains contact.

clue.text: This month in an abbreviated way

definitions.text: This month in an abbreviated way

parts.words: This month in an abbreviated way
parts.note: old business-letter style shortened the word for the current month to a four-letter form

explanation.surface: A clerk jots down the date in shorthand.
explanation.walkthrough: In formal letters 'the 5th inst.' meant the fifth of the current month, short for instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped form of instant, the Latin-derived term used in correspondence for the present month.

clue.text: Writer's addition? It may be taken out in theatre

definitions.text: It may be taken out in theatre

explanation.surface: An author's supplement might get cut during a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre of a hospital, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary material at the end of a book; also the small organ removed by surgeons in an appendectomy.

clue.text: Strange oriental lake

parts.note: oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An odd body of water lies somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Chap concealing a weapon in his clothing

indicators.note: the man hides something inside him, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: chap and gent both mean a man
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A man has a gun hidden under his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An item of clothing, any article worn on the body.

clue.text: Prosper and show off

explanation.surface: Thrive and then flaunt your success.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive or grow vigorously; also to wave or brandish something ostentatiously.

clue.text: Heads down! Toast is here

explanation.surface: An order to duck, followed by drinks all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads down' is the literal picture: with the rear end raised, the head is lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinkers' cheer as glasses are tipped and drained; literally the rear raised, head lowered.

clue.text: Monarch ready to draw the line

explanation.surface: A king prepares to set firm limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign who reigns; also a straight-edged strip used to draw straight lines.

clue.text: Congenial address for a ship's captain?

definitions.text: Congenial address for a ship's captain?

parts.words: Congenial address for a ship's captain?
parts.note: sailors' familiar nickname for their skipper, which is also an affectionate term for a father or husband

explanation.definitionFit: Informal nickname for a ship's master, also used of a father or husband.

clue.text: In very short time the river becomes unsafe

parts.note: sec is short for second, a brief moment
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: In a matter of moments a river turns dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Not secure or firmly fixed, so liable to give way or be at risk.

clue.text: Rabies breaks out in the country

indicators.note: an outbreak of disease, read as the word Rabies breaking apart and reforming

explanation.surface: An outbreak of a deadly disease occurs in some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan nation with its capital at Belgrade.

clue.text: Reasonable desert island with lake

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A barren island with a lake could hardly be more sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun describing the island but is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Based on logic and sound judgement, sensible.

clue.text: I'm about to run? Must be an error

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of I'm are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
sprint and run both mean race fast

explanation.surface: Someone about to dash off fears they've made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it turns I'M round to MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A typographical slip, a wrongly printed letter or word.

clue.text: Showing a number under the harbour light

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming after in the answer

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ray is a beam of light
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A figure stands beneath a lighthouse beam at the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Depiction or representation, as an actor's showing of a character.

clue.text: A short verse on the Shannon river

explanation.surface: A brief poem about Ireland's longest river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shannon is Ireland's longest river; the city of Limerick stands on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-line comic poem; also an Irish city and county on the Shannon estuary.

clue.text: It's pitiful when dad gets the twitch

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: It's sad to see a father develop a nervous spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousing pity or sadness; also feeble or inadequate.

clue.text: Tells of twinges after exercise

indicators.note: twinges come after exercise, so that piece follows in the answer

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
aches are twinges of pain

explanation.surface: Someone describes the pains felt after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tells of' means informs on, as a grass does, not describes.
explanation.definitionFit: To peach is old slang for informing against an accomplice.

clue.text: British sailors occupy a border town in Holland-site of WWII battle

definitions.text: town in Holland-site of WWII battle

indicators.note: sailors occupying a place sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: British naval forces seize a Dutch frontier town, scene of a famous battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch city on the Rhine, scene of the 1944 Allied airborne assault.

clue.text: Man admitting set up is kind of cross

indicators.note: letting something in, so the man holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word set is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A man confesses that he was framed and is rather angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reads as framed but is SET reversed to TES; 'cross' is not angry but a cross shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-pointed emblem of the Knights of Malta is one variety of cross.

clue.text: Their acts are well-known

parts.note: the book of Acts in the New Testament describes the deeds of Jesus's twelve followers

explanation.walkthrough: 'acts' suggests stage performers, but the Acts are the biblical book.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve disciples sent out by Jesus to spread his teaching.

clue.text: Image to carry to top of mountain

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A statue is hauled to a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem or symbol revered by a clan, such as on a totem pole.

clue.text: Unnatural cunning

explanation.surface: Deviousness that seems forced.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrived or artificial in manner; also crafty and sly, like the Artful Dodger.

clue.text: Illegally fix games of snooker

definitions.meaning: plural here, but each single game of snooker is called by one word

explanation.surface: Someone rigs a run of snooker matches.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up someone falsely for a crime; also a single game in snooker or bowling.

clue.text: The French doctor may be frisky

definitions.note: a young creature known for skipping about, rather than an adjective

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor from France might be feeling playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Young sheep are proverbially playful, gambolling in spring fields.

clue.text: He has skill and courage

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A man possesses both talent and bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery or spirit, as in 'take heart'.

clue.text: Anyway, it's where the customs may look

definitions.text: it's where the customs may look

explanation.surface: Customs officers search bags regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless, at all events; also literally inside some suitcase, where officials search luggage.

clue.text: Persuade it's fantasy

explanation.surface: Convince someone that something is imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, to cause someone to accept something; also pretending or imagination.
